bullets.title: META: Q3 beat, equity raise looming, Muse gains 10M users but capex scrutiny sinks stock -9%
bullets.body: META posted Q3 revenue of $64.60B (+26.1% y/y, beat) with ad impressions +10% and price per ad +14%; Q4 guided $73-76B (+22-27% y/y). Muse personal agent hit 10M+ UCAN downloads in 1.5 months with 25% daily engagement and shopping as top use case. However, FY26 capex narrowed to $135-145B (high end), management flagged 'hundreds of billions' in multi-year financing needs, FCF turned negative (-$2.1B in Q3), and non-voting Class C shares announced for January 2027 equity raise—stock fell ~9% WTD. Five-year CDS hit all-time high of 119bp.

bullets.title: NVDA: Supply chain capacity expanding 2.5x; Rubin delay to Q2 2027 cited; GTC Berlin constructive on 2027 demand
bullets.body: NVDA announced multi-billion dollar capacity agreements (Amkor, IBIDEN, KYEC, SPIL, Samsung Electro-Mechanics) to expand substrate capacity 2.5x over three years and double semiconductor testing capacity 2026-2027. However, multiple sources flagged Rubin mass production delayed to Q2 2027 (vs late Q4/early Q1 buyside expectations). GTC Berlin showcased strong 2027 demand signals; Jensen Huang said neocloud demand is 'off the charts' but capital is scarce. Hedgeye removed NVDA long on Rubin delay and neocloud financing stress.

bullets.title: WDC: Monster beat/raise; HDD supply-demand imbalance persists through CY31 visibility; stock underreacted
bullets.body: WDC F1Q27 revenue $4.38B (+5.8% vs consensus), EPS $4.64 (+12.9%), gross margin 58.1% (+240bps above consensus). F2Q guided $5.1B revenue (+11.6% above Street) and 60-61% gross margins. Management highlighted demand visibility through CY2030-31 across hyperscalers, neoclouds, AI labs, and physical-AI applications; HAMR volume shipments targeted 1H CY27. Sell-side 73% Buy with avg PT ~$624, implying 82% upside. Stock received little reward on print, down ~4-6% in initial reaction—Citi cut PT to $660 (from $740), Morgan Stanley $668.

bullets.title: TXN: Record September-quarter beat on data center and industrial recovery; analog pricing power building
bullets.body: TXN F3Q revenue $6.06B (+2.0% above consensus), EPS $2.62 (+7.4%), gross margin 64.2% vs 61.6% expected. F4Q guided $5.80-6.30B and EPS $2.45-2.79, both above consensus on continued above-seasonal growth from industrial, data center, and auto. Data center grew ~70-75% y/y. Analysts expect TXN to raise prices on analog customers in 2027 as foundry capacity tightens; prior cycle GM peak was 69-70% at lower revenue, implying meaningful upside. Wolfe added GFS to Alpha List as adjacent analog beneficiary.

bullets.title: SPOT: Q3 in-line, Q4 gross margin guidance better-than-feared; Morgan Stanley raises PT to $700
bullets.body: SPOT Q3 premium subs +6M (ahead of +5M guide), gross margin 33.0% beat guidance, operating income €672M in line. Q4 guided €820M operating income (beat) and 33.8% gross margin (+80bps q/q). Ad revenue tracked double-digit growth in 2H26. Morgan Stanley raised PT to $700 (from $640) on peaking opex, AI remix monetization ahead, and 30x FY28 FCF; stock +11% on week. Mizuho and KeyBanc also raised targets.

bullets.title: NFLX: Q3 in-line but Q4/FY26 guidance disappoints; ad revenue cut to $2.7B; content leadership shakeup
bullets.body: NFLX Q3 EPS $0.87 beat guidance/consensus, revenue in-line. Q4 guided below consensus on EPS ($0.67 vs $0.73) and margins; FY26 ad revenue cut from ~$3B to $2.7B due to slower ad product rollout and partner integrations. New CCO Peter Rice (ex-Walt Disney) brought in; film chief Dan Lin dismissed. Stock -6.7% WTD; Wolfe downgraded to peer perform; Morgan Stanley cut PT to $77 (from $80), maintains OW.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Q3 beats on EBITDA/EPS/FCF; broadband losses and theme park weakness persist; NBCU spin on track for mid-2027
bullets.body: CMCSA Q3 revenue $29.30B beat ($29.22B cons), EBITDA $9.11B beat ($8.89B), EPS $1.07 beat ($0.99). Broadband net losses -144K slightly better than estimates but 4Q seen at -218K on fiber competition pressure. Peacock EBITDA swung to +$261M vs -$217M a year ago. Theme parks EBITDA -17% YoY on Orlando softness. NBCU spinout on track mid-2027. Wolfe maintains Peer Perform; KeyBanc keeps Underweight ($18 PT).

bullets.title: T: Q3 beats broadly, raises FY26 EPS guidance to $2.40, lowers capex; SpaceX wireless threat sends stock -7%
bullets.body: AT&T Q3 service revenue +3.8% y/y, EBITDA +5.4%, fiber net adds +442K (beat), postpaid ARPU +4.0% y/y. Raised FY26 EPS guidance to ~$2.40 (from $2.25-2.35). Lowered 2027-2028 capex to $22-23B (from $23-24B). Stock fell ~6-7% as SpaceX reaffirmed plans for US terrestrial wireless network via 80,000+ cell sites—Morgan Stanley maintains OW with $25 PT (cut from $28), viewing SpaceX threat as overreaction.

bullets.title: CLS: Expected to beat September quarter and guide strongly for December; CY27 EPS target ~$19
bullets.body: UBS (Buy, $430 PT) expects CLS to beat September quarter and guide strong December quarter on hyperscaler switch/TPU demand. October investor day may outline ~$19 CY27 EPS with 30%+ CCS growth. CLS FY27 revenue consensus ~$38.9B (+80% y/y above Street's $35.7B per analyst). Post-earnings calls with JPMorgan analyst scheduled Oct 28.

bullets.title: GLW: 3Q expected beat on Enterprise optical strength; buy-side bar requires Springboard 2028 update
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects GLW 3Q revenue ~$5.04B and EPS ~$0.90 vs consensus $0.88; Enterprise segment growing >75% y/y on hyperscaler demand. Consensus: $5.03B revenue, $0.88 EPS. Management targeting $30B Springboard revenue by 2028; buy-side needs new targets to drive incremental upside. JPM trimmed PT to $165 (from $170), Neutral. UBS Buy with $201 PT; options imply ~9.7% move.

bullets.title: BE: Beat and raise for third consecutive quarter; CCUS opportunity and Oracle Project Jupiter read-through bullish
bullets.body: Bloom Energy raised FY26 guidance to $4.4-4.6B revenue (+122% y/y) with backlog growth outpacing revenue. Operating leverage faster than expected; capacity expansion to 5+ GW with $5.8B supplier commitments. Morgan Stanley raised PT to $335 (from $310). Oracle's Project Jupiter 35% emissions reduction cited as likely driven by BE fuel cell CCUS integration—BE's direct-current architecture enabling lower-cost carbon capture.

bullets.title: INTC: Seven consecutive financial beats; server CPU supply tight from agentic AI; JPM upgrades to Neutral
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded INTC to Neutral (from Underweight) with $85 PT. Jefferies notes INTC has seven consecutive quarters exceeding financial expectations, with server CPU demand outpacing supply from agentic AI and inference. Diamond Rapids (1Q27) closing performance gap with AMD Venice (4Q26). Evercore notes CPU ASPs rising 15-20% q/q. INTC still carries $8-10 CY29-30 earnings power per Wolfe but execution risk limits conviction.

bullets.title: NOW: JPM bullish into 3Q with ~200bps cRPO beat expected; KeyBanc contrarily maintains Underweight
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects ServiceNow 3Q cRPO beat of ~200bps translating to low-20% reported growth; AI ACV on track to exceed $1.5B target with 10-25% deal size expansion at renewals. Federal revenue pullforward creates favorable comparisons. KeyBanc maintains Underweight ($85 PT) on slowing bookings and acquisition integration headwinds. Wolfe sees Q3 as key test for reacceleration.

bullets.title: CRM: Acquires Braze for $5.66B (60% premium) to bolster marketing automation; mixed reception
bullets.body: Salesforce announced definitive agreement to acquire Braze for $47.50/share in all-cash deal (~$5.66B EV, ~5x CY27 revenue). No change to FY27 guidance; deal closes FY28 pending regulatory/shareholder approvals. CRM stock fell ~3% on announcement on concerns about organic growth pace and antitrust risk (BRZE lists CRM as competitor). JPM maintains Overweight; KeyBanc sees strategic fit but sector weight.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY sportsbook GGR +79% y/y on strong hold; UBS Buy at $48 PT; Week 6 NFL favorable for operators
bullets.body: NY OSB handle growth +5% y/y (week ending Oct 18); GGR hold +410bps y/y to 10.0%, driving +79% GGR growth. October MTD GGR +24% y/y. UBS maintains Buy with $48 PT (17x 2028E EBITDA). Week 6 NFL estimated hold 10-12% as ~46% of favorites won (tailwind). DKNG NY market share 32-33%, down slightly from prior year as Fanatics (11%) gained.

bullets.title: CRWV: Goldman upgrades to Buy ($106 PT) but credit stress intensifies; unsecured bonds yielding ~16%
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs upgraded CRWV to Buy (from Neutral) cutting PT to $106 from $139, citing contract economics and underestimated IRR upside. However, unsecured bond spreads widened ~300bps since late August; stock down 30%+ past month. Morgan Stanley cut to Equal-Weight ($70 PT). Multiple sources flag CRWV needs $24-37B additional debt to reach 3.3GW capacity target; OpenAI concentration risk and DDTL financing uncertainty for enterprise customers highlighted as key risks.

bullets.title: ORCL: AI World investor day Oct 28 expected to raise FY30 revenue target above $90B; buy-side positive
bullets.body: JPMorgan and Citi expect Oracle to raise FY30 revenue guidance (from $225B) at the Oct 28 AI World investor day, with OCI growing from <20% to >70% of revenue by FY30. Multi-cloud database revenue grew +353% y/y in F1Q27. Mizuho dinner with Deloitte Oracle partner signals strong OCI momentum. Key risk: capacity delays at Project Jupiter and Lighthouse data centers (power, permitting). Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: ACN: PT raised to $300 at UBS on AI/cybersecurity tailwinds; Baird downgrades to Neutral despite PT raise
bullets.body: UBS raised ACN PT to $300 (from $278) at Buy rating, citing cybersecurity tailwinds, Gemini Launchpad federal deployments, and SAP Cloud +25% y/y read-through. Baird downgraded ACN to Neutral (from Outperform) raising PT to $252. Stock had run 12 consecutive days prior (+~35% over period). ACN also exploring sale of China operations (up to $1.5B) which could fund M&A target.

bullets.title: HUBS/WIX: Software outperforms as AI trade unwinds; both named as rotation buy candidates by OPCO
bullets.body: HUBS gained +17.3% weekly (per StreetAccount index recap) as software (IGV +5.73-6.0%) dramatically outperformed semis (SOX -3.2-6.7%) during the week's AI unwind. OPCO's Wald upgraded Software/Commercial Services to Overweight and named HUBS and WIX as software rotation buy candidates after semis downgraded to Market Weight following 18-month advance. SaaS index at 6.1x FY+2 EV/Sales; Security at 9.3x.

bullets.title: AMZN: MS elevates to Top Pick ($350 PT); AWS 'sold out past 2028'; AWS revenue expected ~44% y/y in Q3
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised AMZN to Top Pick with $350 PT (from $335) targeting 2027-28 AWS high-40s% EBIT margins. Jassy confirmed AWS compute sold out through 2028; AWS backlog at $496B with AMZN increasing NVDA GPU purchases to 3M chips adding ~2GW/1GW compute in 2027/28. Hedgeye also moved AMZN to buy column. Buyside tracking Q3 AWS at ~44% y/y vs consensus ~37%.
